title: How the GitHub Copilot coding agent works | GitHub Checkout
summary: GitHub demo of the Copilot coding agent: assign issues, background PRs, MCP context, review loop.

assertions.quote: most of the time I'm going to get a PR that's good and ready to go

verdicts.note: Background agents do produce usable PRs for well-scoped chores, but merge rates vary widely and many PRs need iteration; 'most of the time' is optimistic.

475 of 567 Claude Code PRs (83.8%) across 157 open-source projects were merged, statistically lower than 516 of 567 matched human PRs (91.0%); agent-assisted PRs are mostly mergeable, but these are developer-driven Claude Code sessions rather than background agents assigned routine issues.

assertions.quote: Hopefully this is going to be the end of tech debt

verdicts.note: Evidence so far shows AI adoption adding duplication and churn; agents can pay down some debt, but they also create it.
AI commits fix about as many smells as they introduce, but they add more correctness and security issues than they fix, and 22.7% of introduced issues persist for months.

assertions.quote: let Copilot take over the boring stuff

verdicts.note: Benchmarks and field studies show strong performance on well-specified, common tasks and weaker results on context-heavy, novel logic.

METR 2025 RCT: developers report AI lacks tacit repository knowledge (e.g. backwards-compat edge cases, where to make edits), behaving like a new contributor; qualitative support for struggling with context-dependent logic, but 'handles routine well' is not shown in this setting.

AI commits fix slightly more code smells than they introduce (net -7,069) but introduce more correctness (+3,742 net) and security issues (+7,342 net) than they fix, which the authors read as AI handling simple, repetitive patterns but not changes needing deeper understanding of program logic; this is static-analysis evidence, not a test of business-context tasks.

AI-devs favoured simple refactorings (inline/rename variable, annotations) while non-AI devs did more structural ones (Extract Class, Move Method, Extract-and-Move only by non-AI); suggestive group-level pattern with large individual variation.

Expert use accelerates routine implementation while retaining architectural reasoning; domains with complex data pipelines or tightly coupled system logic are associated with correctness and verification challenges, but the domain evidence is thin (data/ML in 2 sources).
Anthropic: engineers delegate low-complexity, self-contained work and keep tasks needing team-specific tacit knowledge, citing the 'cold start' problem as the biggest blocker.

On deliberately popular, well-trodden tasks (games, CRUD apps, REST clients) where 'modern LLMs shine', AI roughly doubled task completeness. This supports the routine-coding half only; complex, context-dependent work was not tested.

GPT-4 solved every easy task but missed 2 of 5 harder algorithmic tasks, consistent with weaker performance on complex logic. The hard tasks were competition puzzles, not business- or system-context tasks.
